message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS.  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, the **Compute Engine API** turned on, and the **GPU API** enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` and `gcloud services enable cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com`).  
> * The GPU type you’re looking for is `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> * The instance must be created in a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Replace <PROJECT_ID> and <ZONE> with your values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

gcloud config set project "$PROJECT_ID"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1` attaches one RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the instance running during maintenance events. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers). |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a script on first boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you want to automatically install the NVIDIA driver, create a `startup.sh` file with the following content and reference it as shown above:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a custom application), you can POST a JSON payload to the `instances` endpoint.

```bash
# Replace placeholders
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# JSON body
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\\napt-get update\\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "maintenancePolicy": "MIGRATE"
}
EOF

# Make the API call (requires OAuth 2.0 token)
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Notes on the JSON payload

- **`machineType`**: Full resource path to the machine type.  
- **`accelerators`**: Specifies the GPU type and count.  
- **`disks`**: Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image).  
- **`metadata.startup-script`**: Optional script to run on first boot (installs NVIDIA driver).  
- **`serviceAccounts`**: Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access.  
- **`maintenancePolicy`**: Keeps the instance running during maintenance events.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project has billing enabled. |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API & GPU API enabled. |
| ✅ | Zone supports GPUs (`us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.). |
| ✅ | GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` is available. |
| ✅ | You have the necessary IAM permissions (`roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`). |

Once the instance is up, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<EXTERNAL_IP>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy computing!
